title: W dużych sklepach
title_en: Plural adjectives in the Locative · -ych again
note:
C1 Block 2, unit 2 (C1-SPINE O2) — the plural adjective's second case, and the course's "same ending, another job" idiom on its FIFTH turn (inst_identity -> inst_z -> inst_transport -> b2_adj_inst -> here).

ZERO NEW FORMS IN THE WHOLE UNIT, so teaches_lemmas is legitimately empty on the copular_future / adj_inst / ze_clauses / passive / existential_tense convention. dobrych, nowych, malych, duzych were all taught one node earlier by c1_adj_pl_gen [182]; every noun is a Locative plural b2_loc_pl [152] already owns; every governor (w, na, o) has been in the course since A1/A2. The unit's entire content is that a string the learner produced last unit is now correct in a second place.

WHAT THIS UNBLOCKS: b2_loc_pl's digest flagged "in the big cities" as unsayable, and nine consecutive B2 units shipped bare-noun under B2-SPINE O3. w duzych miastach is now buildable, and this node is the second instalment of paying that back.

THE SPINE'S OWN ILLUSTRATION IS UNBUILDABLE AND WAS REPLACED, not smuggled in. C1-SPINE's Block 2 table offers "W duzych sklepach. Mysle o starych filmach." The first half is fine. The second half is dead on both words: check_new.py reports starych NEW (c1_adj_pl_gen deliberately dropped stary from its four-adjective set, so no plural oblique of it exists) and filmach NEW (b2_loc_pl's eleven nouns do not include film). The o-governor row is carried by o duzych miastach instead. This is the same class of catch B2 hit repeatedly with its own spine illustrations (Mysle o dobrym filmie, Jade z mila siostra).

THE NOUN LIST IS HARD-LIMITED TO ELEVEN and that shaped every sentence. b2_loc_pl taught exactly domach, sklepach, hotelach, bankach, szkolach, firmach, gazetach, miastach, biurach, mieszkaniach, biurkach. filmach, parkach, kotach, ksiazkach, oknach and telefonach are ALL verified NEW and appear nowhere, which killed several natural draft sentences.

na APPEARS EXACTLY ONCE, and the reason is lexical rather than a scope choice: biurkach is the only one of the eleven that takes na (na biurku, a2_house). The three-governor slide therefore carries one row per governor and the match board weights w heavily. Named here so a later reader does not read it as under-coverage.

THE SINGULAR CONTRAST IS THE UNIT'S SPINE AND IT IS FULLY OWNED. b2_adj_loc taught dobrym/nowym/malym/zimnym and b2_adj_gen taught dobrej/nowej/malej, so the -ym vs -ej choice can be shown honestly and then collapsed: the plural has nothing to choose. Slide 2 runs all three genders down the page for that one payoff.

DISTRACTOR CATCH, the same one c1_adj_pl_gen hit one node earlier and worth restating because it recurs: duzy has NO taught singular oblique. duzym, duzego and duzej are all verified NEW. So every singular row of every table and every singular distractor in the quiz uses dobry / nowy / maly, never duzy — duzy appears only in the plural forms this block owns (duze, duza, duza-instrumental, duzych) and in the quantity word duzo. AGENTS bans fabricated non-words as distractors; an untaught real form is the same failure one step further along.

mieszkania, biurka, mieszkan, firm and biurek are ALL verified NEW and appear nowhere - which is why quiz items 5, 7 and 11 take a grammatical SINGULAR as their sharpest distractor (w malym mieszkaniu, na malym biurku, o nowej szkole) rather than a plain-plural one. That turns out to be the better item in any case: the distractor is real Polish saying something else, which is the discrimination the unit actually needs.

FENCED, and this is the single easiest fence in C1 to break by accident because the three strings are so close (C1-SPINE, Standing fences): NO -ymi anywhere, slides or distractors (c1_adj_pl_inst owns it, next node); NO plural-Dative -ym (c1_adj_pl_dat owns it). Note carefully that -ym DOES appear here, and legally: it is the SINGULAR masculine/neuter Locative b2_adj_loc [136] taught, used in exactly that job, and the unit needs it for the collapse. The homograph is real and is one node away - the same string will be a plural Dative in c1_adj_pl_dat - so that unit must name the collision rather than assume it.

VIRILE forms of every kind are out (c1_adj_pl_virile owns them), so no person noun takes an adjective. ludzie appears once as a bare subject with no adjective on it (Ludzie mieszkaja w nowych domach), which is b2_loc_pl's own sentence shape and does not touch the fence. The honest fact, same as last node: the Locative plural has NO virile split either, so w dobrych lekarzach would have been correct - it is held out anyway so the block says nothing at all about people-plurals before the unit that owns them. -ich (wysokich, drogich) is out too; every adjective here is a hard stem.

PISANIE: eight three-word prepositional phrases. The Locative does not exist without its governor - a bare "dobrych hotelach" is not something anyone says - so the minimal pattern unit for this case INCLUDES the preposition, which is exactly the shape AGENTS names when it lists "w domu" as a Pisanie pattern phrase. Three words, a pattern phrase and not a composed sentence, so typed whole under the James 2026-08-06 cap and its composition refinement. Nothing added to the repair queue. Answers checked for duplicates under the engine's own norm(): all eight distinct, with w duzych miastach and o duzych miastach separated by their governor.

intro.title: The same ending, a second job
intro.title_pl: dużo dobrych sklepów → w dobrych sklepach
intro.body: Last unit gave you -ych for the Genitive plural. It is not a Genitive ending — it is the plural adjective ending, and the Locative is its second job. After w, na and o, which have taken the Locative since A1, the adjective in front of a plural noun is the same string you already produce. There is nothing new to learn here, only somewhere new to put it.

intro.title: The choice the plural takes away
intro.body: In the singular the Locative asked you a question every time: -ym for masculine and neuter, -ej for feminine. In the plural there is no question. One string covers all three genders, exactly as it did in the Genitive.

intro.title: All three trigger words, unchanged
intro.body: No new trigger comes with this ending. The three words that put a noun in the Locative are the three you have always had, and none of them behaves differently in front of a plural.

examples.en: There are a lot of newspapers in the big shops.
examples.pl: W dużych sklepach jest dużo gazet.

examples.en: Mum is thinking about the big cities.

intro.title: One string, two cases
intro.body: -ych is now doing two jobs, and the adjective looks identical in both. What tells you which case you are in is the word in front: dużo and nie ma give you the Genitive, w, na and o give you the Locative. The noun behind the adjective moves differently in each — sklepów against sklepach — so the pair is never actually ambiguous.

examples.en: In the small offices there are no big windows.
examples.pl: W małych biurach nie ma dużych okien.

match.en: There are a lot of newspapers in the big shops.
match.pl: W dużych sklepach jest dużo gazet.

match.en: I'm thinking about the big cities.
There are a lot of shops in the big cities.
match.pl: W dużych miastach jest dużo sklepów.

match.en: We're talking about the new schools.
There are big windows in the new flats.
match.pl: W nowych mieszkaniach są duże okna.

match.en: There are a lot of books in good schools.
match.pl: W dobrych szkołach jest dużo książek.

match.en: I'm talking about the good companies.
There are phones on the small desks.
In the small offices there are no big windows.
match.pl: W małych biurach nie ma dużych okien.

quiz.explain: Both words carry the Locative plural — -ych on the adjective, -ach on the noun. sklepów is the Genitive you learned last unit and belongs after dużo, not after w.
domach is a Locative plural, so the adjective takes the one plural ending. nowym would be right for a single house.
The new ending is for plurals only. One house is still the singular Locative from B2, and nothing about this unit changes it.
o takes the Locative and miastach is plural. dużo is a different word altogether — the quantity, not the size — and it never changes shape.
The last option is good Polish but says something else — in one small flat. Both words have to be plural or neither is.
dobre hotele is the plain plural, the shape English invites because English changes nothing after "in". w always moves what follows it.
na takes exactly the same Locative w takes. Changing the trigger word changes nothing about the endings.
szkoła is feminine, so in the singular this would be dobrej. In the plural the gender stops mattering.
The plural erases the choice between -ym and -ej, but only in the plural. A single feminine noun still takes -ej.

quiz.prompt: In the small offices there are no big windows. →
choices: W małych biurach nie ma dużych okien.
W małych biurach nie ma duże okna.
W małym biurach nie ma dużych okien.
W małych biurach nie ma dużych okna.
quiz.answer: W małych biurach nie ma dużych okien.
quiz.explain: Two different cases in one sentence and the adjective string is the same in both: biurach is Locative after w, okien is Genitive after nie ma. Only the nouns tell them apart.

quiz.prompt: There are big windows in the new flats. →
choices: W nowych mieszkaniach są duże okna.
W nowych mieszkaniach są dużych okien.
W nowym mieszkaniach są duże okna.
W nowych mieszkaniu są duże okna.
quiz.answer: W nowych mieszkaniach są duże okna.
quiz.explain: Only the phrase after w moves. duże okna is the subject of the sentence and nothing is asking it to change — the second option puts it in the Genitive for no reason.
The last option is correct Polish for one school. o behaves like w and na: it never changes, and everything after it does.

type_items.explain: szkoła is feminine and it makes no difference — the plural adjective ending is the same one the masculine nouns take.
The same phrase as the fourth item with a different trigger in front. w and o put the noun in the same case, so nothing after them differs.
